function: Excluded for function: the learned model only classifies hand gestures from WiFi CSI Doppler spectrograms (sensing application, p. 1 abstract and p. 7-8); no beam, waveform, resource or other communication function is learned.
notes: Exclusion code function. OneSense is a WiFi-based gesture recognition (WGR) system: p. 1 abstract "WiFi-based gesture recognition (WGR)" and p. 4 Sec. IV, where the pipeline cleans CSI, extracts Doppler frequency shift and trains a CNN feature extractor with spatial pyramid pooling by aug-meta learning (p. 7-8) to classify unseen gestures from one sample. The learned element is a sensing classifier (gesture classes, accuracy metric, p. 9); it does not design beams, waveforms or resources that serve sensing and communication (area 5) and does not solve detection, channel estimation or feedback, beamforming or RIS configuration, OTFS, NTN or over-the-air federated aggregation. The ISAC claim is only that the sensing model accepts variable-size CSI taken from the packets of an ordinary WiFi router (case study, p. 12: "a WiFi router keeps communicating with some terminal devices"), so nothing learned acts on the communication link. The main setup is one single-antenna transmitter and four three-antenna Intel 5300 receivers at 5.54 GHz (p. 9), with no RIS. Rules 1 to 4 do not apply: it is a research article, it proposes and evaluates a method, the model is learned, and it is not routing, scheduling or similar.
